justification: All three round-1 table failures are confirmed fixed on a real mobile screenshot check at 390 px, in both light and dark, and none of them regress the fix that round 1 demanded. The methods table (mobile-light/dark part05) is now Method/Safe/Idempotent, three narrow columns that fit with margin to spare, with the former fourth column ('Typical use') moved to a clean bulleted list directly below it — nothing is cut. The status-code table (part10) is Class/Name, two columns, fully visible, with 'Meaning' moved to a bulleted list of short phrases right after it. The previously-worst offender, the HTTP/1.1-vs-2-vs-3 table (part17), is now Version/Header encoding only, two columns, comfortably inside the 390 px viewport with visible cell padding on both sides — and the load-bearing content that 250 words of prose depended on ('Where head-of-line blocking is left') is now a three-item bulleted list titled 'Connections and head-of-line blocking, version by version' immediately under the table, so the reader hits that fact before the explanatory prose rather than after failing to scroll for it. This is the strongest table treatment in the article now: table for the compact facts, prose-length facts as bullets, no reliance on horizontal scroll a phone reader is never cued to make. The minor repeated-boilerplate issue is also resolved: 3 of the 5 server programs (families, caching, cookies) are now collapsed behind a `<details><summary>Full program</summary>` that renders correctly collapsed by default in every screenshot checked, in both themes, immediately followed by a clearly labeled 'C# / Excerpt' badge code block holding only the new logic (the Expect/100-continue handling, the Etag/If-None-Match check, and the cookie Set-Cookie/Cookie logic respectively) — each excerpt is short, self-contained, and meaningfully different from the previous program's excerpt, so a reader who has already seen ReadHead/ReadBody twice is not forced to scroll past it a third, fourth and fifth time. Exercise solutions (checked exercise 1 and exercise 5, one per theme) stay correctly collapsed behind 'Show solution' with no visual leakage. Lighthouse held at 90/100/100/100, matching round 1's 91 within noise; the sub-90 driver (FCP/bf-cache) is a generic dev-server characteristic present in round 1 too, not a regression introduced by splitting tables or adding `<details>` blocks — TBT is 0ms and CLS is 0, so there is no script or layout cost from the round-2 changes. Zero console errors, zero broken links, 0px mobile overflow. The three NEEDS_MARKUS placeholders are the same pre-existing, site-wide author-byline markers round 1 accepted as expected and out of scope; they are unrelated to this branch's changes. Docked from a clean 10 only because the Lighthouse performance score landed exactly at the 90 gate rather than comfortably above it (as round 1's 91 did), and because a rerun to rule out worktree contention was not performed — worth a quick re-check at the final gate when the machine is otherwise idle, per the standing SHELL_NOTES guidance, but not something this round's content changes appear to have caused.
